title: Graph-Native Specs for apg
goal: Make apg able to represent a spec as graph data, authored directly in the LadybugDB graph, rendered back to markdown for review, and implemented and tracked through the same graph that holds the code it describes.

body: No parsing of existing markdown files into the graph — the graph is authored directly.
No code generation from spec/plan graphs.
No persistent spec store — the JSONL is the durable form; the DB is rebuilt from it.
No direct DB mutation outside apg spec — no generic Cypher CREATE.
No change to code scanning or fidelity — Contains is extended, not redefined.
Notes do not replace structured data.
No distributed code-writer agents — a repo defines its own via agent-builder.
cargo test passes; round-trip, render section, and is_apg_source_dir unit tests.
Integration fixture: small Go project + fixture JSONLs scanned; spec/plan nodes, edges, and notes query correctly; graph.jsonl carries the records.
Anchor lifecycle: pending anchor becomes Anchors-to-Future; promote re-points, adds Implements, retires the Future; plan done performs the same transition.
apg spec render produces a valid SPEC-style markdown with feature-grouped requirements.
apg init installs all six agents; writer/reviewer permission separation holds; re-running init is idempotent.
Existing code-graph suite tools still pass on repos with and without specs.
cargo build and the frontend build stay green.
Agent prose check: navigator reads a prose spec and proposes a graph structure; spec-writer materializes; plan-writer authors a plan.
Task checklist round-trip: pending to done via plan done, done to pending via undone, surviving a rebuild.
Review-cycle check: reviewer attaches, writer actions, resolve closes, reject reopens; archive/complete refuse with open feedback.
Agent-builder scaffolds a sample repo's writer suite into .opencode/agents/; re-running updates idempotently.
apg spec init/add/anchor/link/rm round-trip: JSONL written, live DB updated, a rescan rebuild reproduces an identical spec graph.
Anchors resolve to real code nodes; pending anchors are Anchors-to-Future and reported satisfied once the target code lands; promote transitions and archive retires.
Future nodes (kind + target) round-trip through the JSONL and query like any node; the future/ root hosts spec, plan, and future code without collision.
apg spec render derives a full template-style markdown spec from the graph; the render is never editable back into the graph.
apg scan auto-discovers specs, plans, and notes; graph.jsonl includes spec, plan, and note records.
apg_spec_unresolved reports dangling refs, orphans, uncovered ACs, pending anchors, drift, and open feedback; apg_plan_phases reports unsatisfied requirements, Gates cycles, and tasks under review.
The distributed writers/reviewers form the closed cycle with no file write access; codebase-navigator delegates via task.
codebase-navigator reads a provided spec and proposes a faithful graph structure; the spec-writer confirms and materializes it.
apg plan done promotes Builds futures and flips the task to done; complete requires all tasks done and feedback resolved; a task whose future has no code errors.
Existing code-graph behavior is unchanged on repos without specs.
Notes route correctly: spec/Future notes to apg/specs/<project>.jsonl, code notes to apg/notes/<module>.jsonl, both surviving a rebuild.
Feedback routes correctly and round-trips; a Feedback whose target was deleted is reported as drift, never fatal.
agent-builder scaffolds a repo's code-writer suite into .opencode/agents/ with a single edit grant.

Specs today are prose markdown that grow to 1000+ lines; structural facts (requirement ids, dependencies, phase ordering, code anchors, antecedents) are embedded inline. This spec makes the cross-reference structure queryable edges in the same LadybugDB graph as the code.
The pipeline is scanner to ingestor to graph to LadybugDB. Specs are treated as just another graph-fed source, merged into the same DB so spec-to-code queries work in one Cypher space.

Layer-first, data-path-down: the schema, then the serialization + scan ingest (the JSONL layouts everything reuses), then the CLI + lifecycle transitions, then the opencode suite tools, then the agents + apg init distribution. The JSONL is the contract throughout.

Notes route by what they Details: a note on a spec/Future node is project-owned and serializes in the spec JSONL; a note on a code node is repo-level and serializes in apg/notes/<module>.jsonl, one file per owning module.

Dangling depends_on/gates/spec_depends/anchors targets are reported by lint, not silently dropped. A Future whose target code now exists is marked satisfied, never an error; a Future is never auto-created. Promote errors on unresolvable targets rather than guessing.
None.
The graph DB is a rebuildable projection; apg/specs/<project>.jsonl is the committed, write-through durable record that survives a fresh scan.

title: Spec node kinds
body: New NodeKind variants and node tables: Spec, Requirement, Phase, Decision, Future, NonGoal, AcceptanceCriterion, VerificationItem, Note, Feedback, Plan, PlanPhase, Task.

title: Rel tables
body: Contains extended with spec pairs; new Details, Reviews, DependsOn, Gates, SpecDependsOn, Anchors, Implements, Satisfies, Builds rel tables.

title: FQN uniqueness / fail-loud
body: Spec and Future fqns follow the future/<project>... convention; residual FQN collisions panic loudly, never silently overwrite.

title: Durable serialization
body: Committed apg/ dir holds apg/specs/<project>.jsonl and apg/notes/<module>.jsonl; gitignored apg/.trans/ holds everything rebuildable.

title: Write-through authoring
body: Every apg spec mutation is write-ahead: load JSONL, apply, write back, re-ingest against the current code graph; authoring is idempotent.

title: apg spec init
body: Creates the Spec node and apg/specs/<project>.jsonl.

title: apg spec add
body: Adds requirement, future, phase, decision, non-goal, acceptance-criterion, verification, and note nodes with their edges.

title: apg spec anchor/link/rm
body: Add/remove edges and nodes explicitly; anchors accept only resolved code FQNs or existing future/... FQNs — never auto-created.

title: apg spec render
body: Derives human-readable markdown from the graph; the render is a projection, never editable back into the graph.

title: Re-ingest on apg scan
body: apg scan auto-discovers spec/note/plan JSONLs after code ingestion, resolves Anchors/Details/Reviews by FQN; unresolvable anchors become pending Anchors to Future nodes.

title: Export
body: graph.jsonl includes spec node and edge records so the self-contained export covers specs and code together.

title: New opencode tools
body: apg_spec/apg_plan/apg_review suite tools installed by apg init into ~/.opencode/tools/; registered in SUITE_TOOLS.

title: Distributed spec-writer agent
body: A hidden subagent with no file write access that authors specs purely through the apg_spec_* tools.

title: codebase-navigator delegation
body: The navigator gains task permission and delegates spec/plan authoring to the writers; reads a provided spec and proposes a graph structure.

title: apg init installation and ownership
body: apg init installs and owns all six distributed agents in ~/.opencode/agents/; ownership checks stay correct; .gitignore scaffolded.

title: Render section mapping
body: apg spec render maps graph state to the platform template: Goal, Background, Scope, Requirements by feature, Non-Goals, Design, Error Handling, Verification, Acceptance Criteria, Open Questions.

title: apg spec promote
body: The explicit Future to present transition: re-anchor, add Implements, retire the Future; errors on unresolvable targets, never guesses.

title: Derived state, no renaming
body: Requirements keep future/<project>/spec.<id> for life; planned vs delivered is derived from Implements presence; a spec is implemented when every requirement is delivered.

title: apg spec archive
body: Moves a fully-implemented spec's JSONL out of active discovery while Implements edges keep delivered work traceable; refuses with unresolved feedback.

title: Plan node kinds
body: Plan, PlanPhase, and Task nodes under future/<project>/plan with strategy, deliverable, and tier/status fields.

title: Plan rel tables
body: Satisfies (PlanPhase to Requirement), Builds (Task to Future), and Gates (PlanPhase to PlanPhase) edges.

title: apg/.trans/plans/<project>.jsonl
body: The plan's write-through transient serialization; retired when the final phase completes.

title: apg plan CLI
body: init, add phase/task, link, done/undone, complete, render — tasks check off per tier, done promotes Builds futures.

title: Distributed plan-writer agent
body: A hidden subagent that authors the plan graph from the spec graph via apg_plan_* tools; may translate a prose plan.

title: Feedback node + lifecycle
body: A review item with status open/actioned/resolved and disposition; reviewer attaches, writer actions, reviewer resolves or rejects.

title: apg review CLI
body: add, action, resolve, reject, list — the closed writer/reviewer state machine.

title: Done gates
body: Done is derived, never asserted: an artifact is done only when every Feedback on it is resolved; archive and plan complete refuse otherwise.

title: Review agents
body: spec-review and plan-review hold review tools and no authoring tools; the writers hold no review-add/resolve/reject tools — the cycle is closed by permissions.

title: Distributed agent-builder
body: A mode:primary agent with a single edit grant to .opencode/agents/** that scaffolds a repo's code-writer suite tailored to its stack and gates.

summary: The future/ root namespaces spec, plan, and future-code FQNs under future/<project> without collision.
Feedback routes to the artifact JSONL of its review: spec/Future targets to the spec JSONL; plan/task/code targets to the plan JSONL.
